title: Bolster Dog Beds
seo_title: Bolster Dog Beds: An Edge to Lean On | PawLunova
seo_description: Chin on the bottom stair, back against your legs? Bolster dog beds with a raised edge on one to four sides, soft-filled or on foam. Pick their edge.

image.alt: Black and tan dog asleep against the U-shaped bolster of the brown Melbreak dog bed in a living room

intro_html: Head on the bottom stair, back against the wall, chin on your foot. A bolster dog bed gives the dog who leans an edge of their own.
description_html:
A bolster dog bed is for the dog who never quite lies in the middle of anything. They wedge their back against the skirting board, rest a chin on your shoe, or lie with their spine pressed to the side of the sofa. Leaning is how they switch off, and a bolster gives that habit a place of its own: a raised, cushioned edge built into the bed.

Which bolster dog bed shape suits them

  • If they want a chin rest and room to stretch, one edge: Watendlath has a pillow bolster along one side and the rest left open. Nocturne's open-sided bolster suits big dogs who start the evening curled and end it stretched out.
  • If they like their back covered and the room in view, two sides: Esthwaite and Bowfell have an L-shaped bolster.
  • If they press in but find climbing hard, three sides: Melbreak, Staveley, Martindale and Rosthwaite leave the front open, so there is something to press into and nothing to climb over. Harrogate frames its cushioned base on three sides too.
  • If they want an edge whichever way they turn, four sides: Borrowdale, Ullswater and Troutbeck. For full walls round a deep, soft middle, see our nest dog beds.

Look at the sleeping area, not just the footprint

A bolster is part of the bed's outside measurement, so the space they actually lie on is smaller. On the Chatsworth Large, the outside is 70 × 55cm and the sleeping area 50 × 45cm. Measure them lying down, add 15 to 20cm, and hold that number against the space inside the bolsters rather than the outside. If it is close, size up.

Fibre bolsters or foam underneath

Kentmere, Ullswater and Loweswater are fibre-filled and Troutbeck soft-filled: yielding, made for snuggling rather than support. If they are stiffening up, choose foam under the bolsters. Chatsworth has a crumb memory foam base; Borrowdale, Melbreak and Staveley pair memory foam with a waterproof liner; Martindale and Rosthwaite layer memory foam over egg-crate foam. Langdale goes further and builds the rim itself from foam, so it holds a defined edge where a stuffed border would sag. Several of the memory foam beds here carry a 5-year no-flatten guarantee on the foam core, subject to the guarantee terms, and their product pages say so. Comfort is the job, not treatment: if your dog is in pain, keep talking to your vet.

The trial on every bolster bed here

You will only really know it is the right edge once they have used it for a while. Each one comes with 100 nights from delivery. If it turns out to be the wrong edge for them, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund; one trial per household, and damage and other exclusions apply. Standard UK delivery is free on orders over £40. The trial page has the detail.

Bolster bed questions

Is a bolster dog bed good for older dogs?

It can be, if the shape lets them walk in. Look for an open front or low entry and foam underneath; Rosthwaite and Martindale leave the front open so there is nothing to step over. Our beds for older dogs gather more.

Will the bolsters go flat?

Fibre-filled bolsters are soft by design, so expect some give. If a firm edge matters, choose Langdale, whose rim is foam rather than loose filling.

What is the difference between a bolster bed and a dog sofa bed?

Mostly shape. A sofa bed is a bolster bed built to look like furniture, usually with arms and a back. See our dog sofa beds.

Torn between an edge and full walls? The Bed Finder works it out from how they sleep.
